name: Clark Bridge (Alton, IL, US 67)
reference_datum: vertical clearance above zero on the Mel Price Upper Gage (RM 201.1), per USACE Supplemental Chart 123A
source_note: USACE Upper Mississippi River Supplemental Chart No. 123A (2020), Mississippi Valley Division. Reference gage: Mel Price Upper Gage, RM 201.1. Elevation, low steel: 485.36' -- elevation, gage zero: 395.48' -- vertical clearance above zero on gage = 66.36 ft. Officially named Clark Highway Bridge on the chart (Coast Guard Light List No. 16240); just upstream of Melvin Price Lock & Dam, opened 1994. Corrects an earlier secondary-source figure of 65 ft (understated by 1.36 ft) and river mile (was 201, chart gives 202.40). CORRECTION (2026-08-11): the previously-assigned alni2 gauge was confirmed live (site showed 6.38 ft, matching USACE RiverGages' Mel Price L&D LOWER gauge, not the UPPER gauge this reference figure requires per the chart's own 'Mel Price Upper Gage, RM 201.1' citation -- Upper read 23.30 ft at the same moment, a ~17 ft difference). Live gauge disabled rather than compute against the wrong pool. A candidate NWPS id (aloi2) was found but couldn't be confirmed as the correct Upper gauge and wasn't used.
notes: Confirmed against the official USACE chart, but no live gauge is currently assigned -- see source_note. Shows "Stage unavailable" until the correct upper-pool gauge is identified.

name: Bayview Bridge (Quincy, IL, US 24)
source_note: Clearance figure from public secondary source, not cross-checked against current USACE chart book or bridge owner permit. All three Quincy-area bridges (Bayview, Quincy Memorial, Quincy Rail) independently return the same 63 ft figure across multiple sources — re-checked specifically because that seemed too coincidental at first. Most likely genuine: all three cross the same reach within about a mile of each other, and USACE/Coast Guard permits typically hold a river reach to one minimum navigational clearance regardless of which structure crosses it, so later bridges built at an already-permitted crossing commonly match the existing minimum rather than getting a fresh number.

A separate MoDOT figure of 14 ft 3 in for this bridge is a different kind of measurement (a roadway/vehicle clearance elsewhere on the structure, not the navigational clearance over water) — not a real conflict once you know that, just two different specs.
